key_provisions_or_claims: Immoral robot behavior (cheating or physical harm) lowered perceived trustworthiness and goodwill in all four experiments.
Liking decreased in three of four experiments.
Willingness to self-disclose fell only when videos showed a robot physically harming a human.
Robot moral behavior did not affect mind perception.
Inconsistent results may reflect harm severity and how moral behavior was operationalized.
annotation.summary_en: Four experiments (vignettes and videos) test how a humanoid robot's moral versus immoral behavior (cheating, physical harm) affects perceived trustworthiness, goodwill, liking, mind perception and willingness to self-disclose. Immoral robots were trusted less; self-disclosure dropped only after physical harm. It is a social-psychology study with no direct governance proposals.
annotation.title_clean: The Role of Perceived Moral Agency of a Humanoid Robot on the Willingness to Self-Disclose, Trustworthiness, Goodwill, and Liking
annotation.title_en: The Role of Perceived Moral Agency of a Humanoid Robot on the Willingness to Self-Disclose, Trustworthiness, Goodwill, and Liking
